articles.title: Delhi State Industrial & Infra floats Rs 2.2-cr pitch for social media and creative mandate
articles.description: New Delhi: The Delhi State Industrial & Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC) has floated an open tender to appoint a Social Media Management & Creative Agency, with the initial one-year contract estimated at Rs 2.20 crore. The engagement can be extended by a year, subject to satisfactory performance and approval by the competent authority. Bids close on August 10, 2026, with technical presentations set for August 13 and financial bids opening August 14. The RFP lays out a wide charter: the selected agency will handle integrated communication support across DSIIDC's work, from industrial infrastructure development and redevelopment of industrial areas to government schemes, MSME promotion, entrepreneurship initiatives, stakeholder engagement. It will also cover exhibitions, workshops, public outreach and other assignments the corporation takes on. On the ground, the mandate spans social media management, digital outreach, content production and website upkeep, alongside photography, videography, corporate communication, branding and creative services, media monitoring and analytics. The deliverables list runs long: press releases, annual reports, brochures, presentations, speeches, campaign films, reels, animations and other multimedia assets. Monthly targets are specific: 50-70 social media posts or creatives, 10-15 short-form videos, 4-6 motion graphics outputs, 10-15 creative designs, and support for up to 10 assigned events or site visits, among other deliverables. The annual ask adds one corporate report, up to four institutional films, up to 12 newsletters, support for major events, workshops and stakeholder consultations, and programme-specific outreach. The growth bar is set at a minimum 5% month-on-month increase in followers or subscribers across DSIIDC's active platforms, alongside gains in engagement metrics like reach, impressions, views, likes, comments, shares and watch time. That said, evaluators will factor in platform maturity, approved content volume, paid promotion and algorithmic shifts before judging performance. To qualify, bidders need to be legally registered in India and hold a valid Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) empanelment, plus an average annual turnover of at least Rs 10 crore over the last three financial years, positive net worth, offices in more than one Indian city, and at least 50 full-time professionals spread across creative, content, digital, research, technology and operations. On the track record front, they'll also need at least three qualifying government or PSU communication assignments, each worth Rs 1.5 crore or more, completed in the previous five years. Selection runs through a Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) process: 70% weightage goes to the technical evaluation, 30% to the financial proposal. That technical score will weigh annual turnover, relevant government assignments, the proposed core team and a technical presentation, and bidders need at least 70 marks to move on to the financial bid stage. The tender, published on July 26, 2026, is currently open .

articles.title: Puri bridge project stalls; villagers cross canal on bamboo makeshift bridge
articles.description: An unfinished bridge in Denua panchayat under Nimapada block of Odisha 's Puri district has become a daily challenge for more than 15 families, who continue to cross the half-built structure by placing wooden planks and bamboo over it. While the contractor blames pending bills for the stalled work, the concerned department cites a shortage of funds, leaving villagers with no safe way to reach the other side. The bridge, being built for Rs 20 lakh to connect Harijan Sahi with the main village, was inaugurated in March. The work continued for a few days before coming to a halt. Since then, residents, including children and elderly people, have been using a makeshift crossing over the canal. During the monsoon , the overflowing water and slippery surface make the journey even more dangerous, especially during medical emergencies. Villagers Demand Immediate Completion Of Bridge A resident, Meena Das, said, “We face a major problem at night, especially during medical emergencies. Students have stopped going out to study because it is too risky to cross the bridge. We appeal to the Deputy Chief Minister to solve our problem. If nothing is done, we will be forced to stage a protest.” Another resident, Santosh Das, said, “It has been more than six months since the tender was awarded, but the bridge is still incomplete. We have placed a ladder just to cross it. During the recent rain, the soil was washed away, and my uncle slipped into the water while crossing. Thankfully, we managed to save him.” Also Read: Jajpur floods turn devastating; 250 villages inundated, over 1 lakh impacted after 7 breaches Contractor Rakesh Senapati said the work stopped because the running bill has not been cleared. Drainage Department SDO Bibhu Bhushan Mallick said the payment remains pending due to a shortage of funds and assured that construction will resume once the government releases the required amount. For the villagers, however, the wait continues, as every trip across the unfinished bridge remains a risk they have no choice but to take.
